help.title: Build an AI product or feature
help.desc: From a business goal to a feature in production: scoping, architecture, the build and an evaluation baseline, so you know it works before your users depend on it. Fixed scope, priced per deliverable.

help.title: Make an LLM system reliable
help.desc: Your RAG or agent works in the demo but behaves differently in production. I find out why: separate retrieval and generation scores, a golden set, LLM-as-judge against a rubric, and checks for prompt injection and PII leaks. You get a ranked failure report and the fixes.

help.title: Lead AI engineering with your team
help.desc: A lead or staff-level engineer working inside your team on a long-term contract: architecture, delivery, a practical way to use AI in development, and direct work with product and leadership on what to build and why.
help.fit: For companies building an AI capability

cases.title: An LLM delivery pipeline that outshipped a 12-person team
cases.problem: The business grew by launching new apps. The team I led, 9 engineers and 3 designers, had plateaued at about 8 apps a week, and adding people added coordination rather than output.
cases.did: I designed and ran a multi-agent pipeline that covers design, code, store assets and promo websites, with model routing by task across Claude, Gemini and OpenAI, independent verification agents, LLM-as-judge audits on a severity rubric, and cost limits per session. I also architected its Google Cloud platform (Gemini and Claude on Vertex AI, Cloud Run, IAP, Secret Manager, Cloud Logging) and multimodal text-and-image search over the company's catalogue of 2,000+ apps, and replaced a paid low-code admin platform with an in-house dashboard, a build-vs-buy call that AI-assisted development made practical.
cases.result: In my last week I shipped 10 production apps in 3–4 days, solo, with one QA engineer checking the builds, at about $6 per app in model APIs.

cases.title: New distribution channels for a portfolio of 200 apps
cases.problem: I owned a portfolio of about 200 mobile apps end to end, from the idea through release to live operations, working with the business owners on budgets and ROI to keep it profitable.
cases.did: On my own initiative I researched Huawei AppGallery and Samsung Galaxy Store, shipped test apps, measured the results and, once the business approved, ran full releases there. I proposed in-app user-acquisition campaigns in Samsung Galaxy Store and owned their technical side: attribution with Adjust and AppsFlyer, ad SDKs and campaign data.
cases.result: Five app stores supplied from one Android codebase with per-store builds. A shared app template made each new app mostly configuration and assets, with 80–90% of the code reused.

cases.title: A security feature in a 20-year-old codebase, on a stack I had never used
cases.problem: Personal access tokens for the REST API of Redmine 6.1.2, a Ruby on Rails application with twenty years of history.
cases.did: I started with code maps, had subagents implement the changes, and re-ran a five-axis verification gate after every fix. No agent graded its own work.
cases.result: 39 issues, 75 recorded attacks and 4,674 lines of tests. The full process record is published next to the code.

process.title: Start from the business number
process.desc: What is it worth if it works, and what does it cost when it fails? That decides the architecture and the budget, including where an LLM is the wrong tool.

process.title: Build the evaluation first
process.desc: A golden set and a scoring rubric come before the feature, so that "better" is a number rather than an opinion.

process.title: Verify independently
process.desc: Generation is cheap; verification is the bottleneck. Every output passes checks that the agent which produced it does not control.

process.title: Hand over something you own
process.desc: The code, the evaluation harness and the documentation stay with you, and so does the knowledge of how it works.

public.title: Enterprise RAG & Agents Handbook
public.desc: A practical, first-principles handbook on production RAG and agentic systems, teaching the why and the failure modes rather than the features.
public.meta: Handbook · since July 2026 · three courses, several languages

public.title: Strata-RAG
public.desc: An open-source RAG engine built evaluation-first: hybrid retrieval with rank fusion, cross-encoder re-ranking, a metadata store for counting and listing questions, an evaluation harness with retrieval metrics and LLM-judge faithfulness, and layered defences against prompt injection and PII leaks.

public.title: strata-insurance-corpus
public.desc: A reproducible, synthetic, multi-format insurance document corpus (born-digital and scanned PDFs, Word, spreadsheets, photos) with a golden evaluation set by construction. Built to benchmark document RAG on enterprise-shaped data.

public.title: I Asked a Frontier LLM to Recover Secrets from My Decompiled Build
public.desc: You cannot judge your own obfuscation, because you already know where everything is. I gave a frontier LLM the decompiled build, had it try to recover the secrets blind, and ran the investigation as an adversarial court so the result could be trusted.

public.title: Eval-First RAG: Use Separate Scores to Triage Failures
public.desc: One end-to-end score shows that answer quality moved, but not what moved it. Scoring retrieval and generation separately turns an unclear regression into a decision about where to look first.

about: I'm a physicist by training. I started out writing C++ simulations for CERN's LHC experiments, then spent more than 20 years building software and leading engineering teams.

I founded a mobile games studio and grew it to a team of seven: I shipped 200+ games as lead engineer, negotiated partnerships with publishers and ad networks, and ran hiring, finances and KPIs. I was brought in as interim COO to stabilise a startup, analysing its profitability and guiding a pivot. For six years I was the lead engineer at a mobile-app company, working with the business owners on budgets and ROI and with the executive team on strategy.
In 2025 I rebuilt my own delivery around AI. The lesson I took from it: generation isn't the bottleneck, verification is.
